extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (postdocs) and Collaborative Research Centre administrators considering the DFG Emmy Noether Programme
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on establishing an Emmy Noether independent junior research group and on associating such a group with a DFG-funded Collaborative Research Centre (CRC), covering funding period, integration, resource sharing, institutional decisions, recruitment, and career incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme purpose — support for early independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Emmy Noether Programme supports researchers in achieving independence at an early stage of their scientific careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdocs gain the qualifications required for a university teaching career during a DFG-funded period, usually lasting five years, in which they lead their own independent junior research group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding period / duration
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG-funded period, usually lasting five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this period postdocs lead their own independent junior research group and gain qualifications for a university teaching career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for leading an independent junior research group
rubrics_metrics.description: Emmy Noether fellows lead their own independent junior research group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership of an independent group is the mechanism by which postdocs achieve early career independence and teaching qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for association with a Collaborative Research Centre (CRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Emmy Noether independent junior research group can be associated with a Collaborative Research Centre at the same location which is conducting research into an appropriate subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Association requires the CRC to be conducting research relevant to the junior group's subject area; association is location‑based (same location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration into an excellent research environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Association with a CRC allows the independent junior research group to be integrated into an excellent research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration aims to embed the junior group within broader institutional research activities and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full membership and shared key resources
rubrics_metrics.description: As a full member of the Collaborative Research Centre Group, the leader of the independent junior research group shares in its key resources (such as funding for guests, travel and events and flat-rate allowances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared resources include explicit examples: funding for guests, travel and events, and flat-rate allowances; membership confers access to these CRC resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRC authority to decide on association
rubrics_metrics.description: The Collaborative Research Centre decides on the association in accordance with its rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Association is subject to the CRC's internal decision-making and governance procedures rather than automatic acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellows may attract their own projects to the CRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently of the association with the Emmy Noether Group, researchers funded under the Emmy Noether Programme can attract projects of their own to the Collaborative Research Centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not formally associated, fellows retain the ability to bring projects into the CRC, supporting research independence and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRC encouraged to recruit and inform suitable candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative Research Centres are encouraged to approach suitably qualified early career researchers and to make them aware of the opportunities and benefits of integrating an Emmy Noether independent junior research group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit expectation for CRCs to proactively engage and inform potential fellows about program benefits and integration possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive: career prospects after successful interim evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: One important incentive to set up an Emmy Noether independent junior research group in association with a Collaborative Research Centre is the attractive career prospects available to group leaders who have successfully passed an interim evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful interim evaluation can lead to enhanced career opportunities; this incentive is highlighted as a motivation for association with CRCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme aim: building up local research structures
rubrics_metrics.description: These opportunities are offered with the aim of building up local research structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association and incentives are explicitly framed as measures to strengthen institutional and regional research capacity and structures.
